transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2025-07-23 15:00 PDT | Duration: 52 minutes | Location: Zoom | Recording: yes
Attendees: Aisha Patel (Redwood AE), Diego Ramirez (Redwood SE), Ellen Cho (Catalyst CTO), Marcus Li (Catalyst SRE), Priya Narang (Catalyst Compliance)

Summary: quick sync for Private VPC pilot — networking stuck on routing rules, small perf regressions after model upgrade, compliance questions around KMS and audit logs, agree next steps for config artifacts and load tests.
Topics: networking & routing, model upgrade results, latency/cost tradeoffs, KMS/audit, next steps
Shared artifacts: pilot-deck link https://redwood.app/pilot/catalyst-deck, benchmark sheet (drive) https://drive.example/pilot-catalyst-bench

Transcript:
[00:00] Aisha: thanks everyone for joining, we have 52 minutes on the calendar. quick agenda — network sync, perf numbers since last upgrade, and security follow-ups.
[00:18] Ellen: hey thanks, yep we mostly want to unblock the routing so we can hit the sustained load test next week.
[00:32] Diego: quick note, we pushed the nginx ingress change you asked for, but we saw two route flaps when the failover exercised across AZs. might be a health-check timing issue.
[00:47] Marcus: yeah we saw TCP resets, possibly from the firewall stateful rules. i changed the idle timeout but need to confirm with corporate firewall team — i can share the exact rules after this call.
[01:05] Aisha: ok that's helpful, do you have the CIDR ranges? we recommended the 10.10.0.0/16 for the private subnets in the doc.
[01:20] Marcus: yes i'll paste them — 10.10.0.0/16 for services, 10.11.0.0/16 for infra, i will also include the transit-gw peering config.
[01:37] Priya: while you're on network, i need to confirm where logs land — remember, audit logs need to be retained 7 years for us. how's that set up?
[01:50] Diego: right now the control plane audit logs are pushed to the customer s3 bucket via cross-account role; we can increase retention there. for node-level syslogs we can stream to your splunk instance or to S3, whatever you prefer.
[02:08] Ellen: s3 is preferred for now, and we need encryption with customer-managed KMS keys.
[02:20] Diego: KMS is supported — we have instructions in the private deploy doc for configuring a customer KMS key (note: the doc's ARN example had a typo last week, fixed in the deck).
[02:36] Aisha: i'll send the corrected doc link after.
[02:40] [03:00] Speaker 1: um sorry, small interruption — about the perf numbers, we ran the model upgrade to v2-quant yesterday, the p95 latency went from around 110ms to 150ms at the 512 token mark under our baseline test.
[03:18] Diego: yes that aligns with our numbers — the quantization tradeoff increased token inference time slightly for certain attention kernels; but overall throughput is up, cost per token down ~18%.
[03:34] Marcus: can you confirm the request pattern? our test has many short requests (avg 64 tokens) and some long ones.
[03:45] Diego: baseline was mixed: 70% short (<=64), 20% mid (65-256), 10% long (>256). the longer requests show better amortization and latency impact is less pronounced.
[04:00] Ellen: for our product, 95% are short so the p95 hit is concerning. is there tuning we can do?
[04:12] Diego: yes — two levers: route short requests to an unquantized variant (higher cost), or adjust batching and KV cache policies so short requests see lower scheduling overhead. we can prototype a routing rule.
[04:33] Aisha: and there's also the Dedicated fallback option if you need strict p95 targets — we'll include pricing for that.
[04:45] Priya: price and SLA please.
[04:50] Aisha: noted. i'll send the Dedicated fallback pricing and the pilot extension options.
[05:00] [05:15] Speaker 2: ok on routing, diego you mentioned nginx; can we see the ingress snippet?
[05:24] Diego: sure i'm sharing screen now — example snippet: proxy_read_timeout 120s; healthcheck path /healthz. (transcription note: some flags may be abbreviated).
[05:40] Marcus: the firewall team requires stateful source nat exceptions for the health checks; otherwise connection tracking kills the session.
[05:50] Diego: we can shift to TCP-level health probes to avoid HTTP timeouts if that helps.
[06:02] Ellen: earlier you mentioned failover across AZs — is the K8s cluster multi-AZ?
[06:12] Diego: yes control plane is multi-AZ; the local nginx ingress lives in each AZ. routing uses a regional LB with cross-zone balancing. we saw flaps when the LB removed targets during a short drain.
[06:28] Marcus: we'll increase connection drain and adjust health probe grace to 30s.
[06:36] Aisha: perfect, action item — Marcus to provide firewall rules and confirm drain settings.
[06:44] Marcus: noted.
[07:00] [07:20] Diego: switching topics — model upgrade telemetry: we collected token-level breakdowns and cost numbers in the bench sheet. p50 stable, p95 regressed for short tokens. cpu/gpu utilization shows steady 70-80% on the pilot nodes.
[07:40] Ellen: what about KV cache warm-up? we saw cold starts after restarts.
[07:48] Diego: currently warm-up is per-node on first request; we can seed cache with a warmup job during deploy to avoid cold p95 spikes.
[08:00] Priya: is cached data in-memory only? how does that affect data residency?
[08:08] Diego: KV cache is in-memory per node, never persisted to disk, so it does not leave your VPC.
[08:15] Priya: ok good. please document that for compliance.
[08:22] Aisha: will do.
[08:30] [09:00] Speaker 3: question on cert rotation — we rotate mTLS certs every 90 days, can Redwood support auto-rotation via our KMS?
[09:12] Diego: yes certs can be rotated via the agent using your KMS for signing; need to test the flow in a staging cluster.
[09:24] Marcus: i'll set up a staging cluster for the test.
[09:30] Ellen: timeline check — we want to run the 72-hour sustained load test starting 2025-07-29. is that feasible?
[09:40] Aisha: yes if routing and firewall items are resolved and we run the pre-checks. we also need a final smoke test 48 hours before.
[09:52] Priya: we need the security checklist sign-off before the sustained test.
[10:00] [10:15] Diego: i will prepare a pre-check script: health endpoints, KV cache warm state, KMS access test, and smoke throughput at target qps.
[10:28] Ellen: please share script in the bench sheet.
[10:32] Diego: will do.
[10:38] [11:00] Aisha: quick note on routing policies — we recommend a policy: route short requests to model-std (no quant), mid/long to model-quant; fallback to model-std if p95 exceeds threshold.
[11:15] Marcus: that sounds reasonable; do you have a sample policy?
[11:20] Aisha: yes i'll add sample to the runbook and send link.
[11:28] [12:00] Diego: also we can do an A/B canary for the upgrade — 5% traffic to quant variant and monitor quality/regressions.
[12:10] Ellen: about quality, we ran a small eval and saw minor tokenization differences but nothing product-breaking. we'll run the larger eval once routing is stable.
[12:24] Priya: please confirm log redaction for PHI — any PHI should be masked before leaving the VPC.
[12:36] Diego: Redwood agent supports custom redaction hooks; we'll share the config snippet.
[12:45] Aisha: action: Diego to share redaction snippet and the helm values.
[12:52] [13:00] Speaker 4: are there any outstanding compliance docs?
[13:06] Priya: i need SOC 2 sys description and encryption attestation.
[13:12] Aisha: we'll share SOC 2 summary and the encryption whitepaper.
[13:18] [14:00] Diego: small comment on metrics — we saw error spikes during the upgrade window when KV cache reset coincided with a burst. that's why warm-up job is important.
[14:14] Marcus: do you have a recommended warm-up window?
[14:18] Diego: 10-15 minutes per node during rolling deploy for our workload; depends on cache size.
[14:26] Ellen: ok.
[14:30] [15:00] Aisha: let's recap next steps and owners — Diego will share config snippets and pre-check script; Marcus to share CIDRs and firewall rules; Priya to confirm SOC 2 items; Aisha will send pricing and the runbook.
[15:18] Marcus: i'll try to get the firewall rules today.
[15:22] Ellen: we'll plan for the sustained test 7/29 and notify you if anything slips.
[15:30] [16:00] Priya: quick question — if we need lower p95 immediately, what's the fastest mitigation?
[16:08] Diego: quickest is routing short requests to unquantized variant or increasing instance size to reduce per-token latency.
[16:18] Aisha: i'll include both options in the pricing note.
[16:24] [17:00] Speaker 1: small aside — competitor check, Catalyst also evaluated Anthropic's hosted offering; they couldn't meet their data residency constraints.
[17:15] Ellen: correct, hosted didn't fit our compliance needs.
[17:22] Aisha: good context.
[17:28] [18:00] Diego: one last technical note: if you opt for Dedicated fallback we can provision GPU pools with pinned models which will give predictable p95 and more aggressive batching.
[18:44] Ellen: please include estimated capacity and lead time.
[18:50] Aisha: will do.
[19:00] [20:00] Wrap / closing:
[20:05] Aisha: thanks all — i'll send notes, updated deck link, and pricing by end of week. next sync same time next week unless we need an ad-hoc to unblock firewall.
[20:18] Diego: i'll upload the pre-check script and ingress snippet to the bench sheet.
[20:26] Marcus: thanks, talk soon.
[20:30] Ellen: thanks everyone.
[20:35] Priya: bye.

Recap (auto): network routing + firewall rules to fix failover flaps; KV warm-up to reduce p95 spikes after upgrades; KMS and audit log retention confirmed; demo of redaction hooks; next steps and owners listed above.

End of transcript.
